newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka, Japan's NTT sign telecom deal.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka, Japan's NTT sign telecom deal.

text.p: Japan's Nippon Telephone and Telegraph Corp signed a $225 million deal on Tuesday to buy a 35 percent stake in the state telecommunications monopoly Sri Lanka Telecom, officials said.
They said the deal, the single largest foreign investment in Sri Lanka, would see the Japanese company take over the management of Sri Lanka Telecom.

"It is the single largest foreign commercial investment Sri Lanka has seen to date," Mano Tittawella, director general of the Public Enterprise Reform Commission (PERC), told Reuters. "The money will be remitted today (Tuesday)," he added.

Under the terms of the strategic partnership agreement between NTT and the government, the Japanese firm will appoint a chief executive officer and several senior executives to supervise the joint venture.
Government officials said Sri Lanka Telecom's entire workforce of more than 8,000 people will be retained.

Sale of Telecom's equity is part of the Sri Lankan government's efforts to privatise the country's loss-making public enterprises to boost its creaking infrastructure and attract foreign investment, government officials said.
